uni-agri-core.title: Agriculture core (B.Sc Agriculture)
uni-agri-core.description: Core B.Sc Agriculture: soil science, agronomy, crop protection, agricultural economics and modern farming in India, with farm numericals and practical labs. Study companion; topics commonly taught in Indian agricultural universities.

courses.title: Soil science: physical properties, water and fertility
courses.summary: Bulk density, porosity, available water capacity and fertiliser calculations.

lessons.title: Lab: Bulk density by the core method

story.title: Soil samples from a Punjab field

scenes.text: A student drives a 100 cm³ core into the soil and oven-dries it.
The dry soil weighs 135 g.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: **Bulk density = dry mass / total volume** (g/cm³). Most mineral soils are 1.1–1.6 g/cm³.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: Use oven-dry mass, not field-moist mass.

activity.prompt: Dry mass 135 g in a 100 cm³ core. Bulk density?

quiz.q: Bulk density of a clay loam is typically

options: higher bulk density than clays often

story.title: How much room for air and water?

scenes.text: Pore space holds air and water for roots.
You find it from bulk and particle density.

steps.title: Formula
steps.body: **Porosity = 1 − (ρb/ρs)**; ρs for mineral soil ≈ 2.65 g/cm³.

steps.title: Aeration
steps.body: Macropores drain; micropores hold water.

activity.prompt: ρb = 1.35 g/cm³, ρs = 2.65 g/cm³. Porosity in %?

scenes.text: A farmer needs to know how much water 60 cm of root zone stores.
Field capacity is 30% and wilting point 15% by volume.

steps.title: AWC
steps.body: **AWC (mm) = (θFC − θPWP) × root depth (mm)**.

steps.title: Management allowed depletion
steps.body: Irrigate before all available water is used; typical allowed depletion is about 50% for many crops.

activity.prompt: FC = 30%, PWP = 15% (volumetric), root depth 60 cm. Available water in mm?

story.title: A Soil Health Card says nitrogen is low

scenes.text: A farmer in Madhya Pradesh receives a recommendation of 120 kg N/ha for wheat.
She must decide how much urea to buy per hectare.

steps.title: Fertiliser grade
steps.body: Urea contains 46% N. **Quantity = nutrient needed / nutrient fraction**.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: 120/0.46 = 260.9 kg urea per ha.

steps.title: Splitting
steps.body: N is usually applied in splits to reduce losses.

activity.prompt: Recommendation 120 kg N/ha; urea is 46% N. Urea needed per ha?

courses.title: Agronomy: seed rate, crop water need and cropping intensity
courses.summary: Seed-rate calculation, crop evapotranspiration, irrigation volumes and cropping intensity.

scenes.text: A farmer wants 66,667 plants/ha of maize.
The seed test shows 90% germination and 1000-grain weight of 300 g.

steps.title: Formula
steps.body: Seed rate (kg/ha) = (plants/ha × seed weight (g)) / (1000 × germination fraction). Add purity correction if needed.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Each seed weighs 0.3 g. 66,667 × 0.3 = 20,000 g = 20 kg at 100% germination. At 90%: 20/0.9 = 22.2 kg/ha.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: Forgetting germination loss gives a thin stand.

activity.prompt: 66,667 plants/ha, 1000-grain weight 300 g, germination 90%. Seed rate?

scenes.text: Reference ET is 5 mm/day at a Rajasthan site.
The crop coefficient at mid-season is 1.15.

steps.title: FAO method
steps.body: **ETc = Kc × ET0**.

steps.title: Kc stages
steps.body: Kc is low at initial stage, peaks mid-season, then falls.

activity.prompt: ET0 = 5 mm/day, Kc = 1.15. Crop evapotranspiration?

quiz.q: 1 mm of water over 1 ha is

scenes.text: A 2-ha plot needs a 50 mm irrigation.
The pump discharge is planned from the volume.

steps.title: Volume
steps.body: Volume = area × depth. 1 ha = 10,000 m².

steps.title: Efficiency
steps.body: Surface irrigation delivers perhaps 40–60% to the crop; drip can exceed 85–90%.

activity.prompt: 2 ha, 50 mm irrigation depth. Water volume?

options: water stored in root zone / water applied

story.title: How intensively is the land used?

scenes.text: A block has 100 ha of net sown area and 180 ha gross cropped area.
You report cropping intensity to the district office.

steps.title: Formula
steps.body: **Cropping intensity (%) = gross cropped area / net sown area × 100**.

steps.title: Meaning
steps.body: 180% means about 1.8 crops per year on average.

activity.prompt: Net sown 100 ha, gross cropped 180 ha. Cropping intensity (%)?

options: better resource use and risk spread

courses.title: Crop protection: IPM, disease incidence and efficacy
courses.summary: Spray dilution, disease incidence, Abbott's correction and the IPM decision sequence.

scenes.text: A label recommends a 0.1% solution at 500 L spray volume per hectare.
A technician must compute product needed. Always follow the actual label.

steps.title: Percent solution
steps.body: 0.1% v/v means 1 mL product per litre of spray fluid.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: 500 L × 1 mL/L = 500 mL = 0.5 L per ha.

steps.title: Safety
steps.body: Read the label, wear PPE, observe waiting periods and never exceed the label dose. This is education, not a prescription.

activity.prompt: 0.1% v/v solution, 500 L spray fluid per ha. Product needed?

options: days between last spray and harvest

scenes.text: A scout checks 200 plants and finds 30 with wilt symptoms.
She reports percent incidence.

steps.title: Incidence
steps.body: **Incidence (%) = infected plants / plants assessed × 100**. Severity is the % tissue area affected.

steps.title: Triangle
steps.body: Disease needs host, pathogen and favourable environment.

activity.prompt: 30 of 200 plants infected. Incidence in %?

You correct for natural mortality.

steps.title: Resistance
steps.body: Rotating modes of action slows resistance.

activity.prompt: Treated mortality 64%, control 10%. Corrected mortality?

options: repeated selection with same mode of action

story.title: A cotton field with bollworm moths

scenes.text: Traps show rising moth numbers in a cotton farm.
The agronomist follows the IPM workflow.

steps.title: Principle
steps.body: IPM combines cultural, mechanical, biological and chemical tactics and uses pesticides only when pest numbers cross the economic threshold.

steps.title: Threshold
steps.body: ETL is the pest density at which control cost equals expected loss.

steps.title: Records
steps.body: Scouting records support better decisions every season.

activity.prompt: Order the IPM steps.
items: Scout fields and use pheromone traps to monitor
Identify the pest and its stage correctly
Compare counts with the economic threshold level
Apply cultural, mechanical and biological controls first
Use a selective label-approved pesticide only if still needed

options: lure pests away from the main crop

courses.title: Agricultural economics: costs, returns and break-even
courses.summary: Benefit–cost ratio, net returns, supply elasticity and break-even yield.

scenes.text: A farmer records ₹60,000 total cost and ₹90,000 gross returns per hectare.
An extension officer computes B:C.

steps.title: Formula
steps.body: **B:C = gross returns / total cost**. A value above 1 means returns exceed cost.

steps.title: Include
steps.body: Count family labour and land rent (imputed) to get honest costs.

activity.prompt: Gross returns ₹90,000/ha, cost ₹60,000/ha. B:C ratio?

scenes.text: A wheat grower harvests 40 q/ha and sells at a hypothetical ₹2,000/q.
Cost of cultivation is ₹55,000/ha.

steps.title: Net return
steps.body: Net return = yield × price − cost.

steps.title: MSP
steps.body: Minimum Support Prices are announced by the Government of India for notified crops; check the current year's list.

activity.prompt: Yield 40 q/ha, price ₹2,000/q, cost ₹55,000/ha. Net return?

story.title: Prices rise, will farmers grow more?

scenes.text: Onion price rises 10%; area sown rises 6% next season.
An analyst finds the elasticity.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: **Es = %Δ quantity supplied / %Δ price**.

steps.title: Cobweb
steps.body: Planting after seeing high prices can crash prices at harvest.

activity.prompt: Price +10%, quantity supplied +6%. Price elasticity of supply?

scenes.text: Cost is ₹60,000/ha; expected price ₹2,000/q.
A bad monsoon threatens yields.

steps.title: Break-even yield
steps.body: **Yield* = total cost / price**.

steps.title: Risk
steps.body: Crop insurance (PMFBY) and diversification reduce income risk.

activity.prompt: Cost ₹60,000/ha, price ₹2,000/q. Break-even yield?

options: value of the best alternative forgone

courses.title: Modern farming in India: drip, remote sensing and solar pumps
courses.summary: Water saving with drip, NDVI from satellite or drone imagery, solar pump sizing and an FPO-setup checklist.

lessons.title: Lab: Water saved by drip irrigation

scenes.text: A farmer uses 1000 mm of flood irrigation per season; a drip trial uses 600 mm.
What is the water saving?

steps.title: Saving
steps.body: **Saving (%) = (flood − drip)/flood × 100**.

steps.title: Fertigation
steps.body: Drip allows nutrients through the same system.

activity.prompt: Flood 1000 mm, drip 600 mm. Water saving in %?

scenes.text: A drone camera records near-infrared and red reflectance for a field patch.
NIR = 0.5 and Red = 0.1.

steps.title: NDVI
steps.body: **NDVI = (NIR − Red)/(NIR + Red)**; healthy vegetation is high (often 0.6–0.9).

steps.title: Context
steps.body: NDVI saturates in dense canopies; ground-truth with scouting.

activity.prompt: NIR = 0.5, Red = 0.1. NDVI?

scenes.text: A farm needs 10 L/s from a borewell with 30 m total head.
Pump set efficiency is 40%.

steps.title: Power
steps.body: Hydraulic power = ρgQH; input power = hydraulic/η.

steps.title: PV array
steps.body: The panel must exceed pump power to cover losses and low sun hours; PM-KUSUM supports solar pumps.

activity.prompt: Q = 10 L/s, head 30 m, overall efficiency 40%. Input power required?

lessons.title: Lab: Capstone – Plan a Farmer Producer Organisation

scenes.text: Chilli growers near Guntur want better prices by selling together.
You help them plan an FPO.

steps.title: Why FPO
steps.body: A Farmer Producer Organisation pools input purchasing, aggregation, grading, storage and marketing.

steps.title: Services
steps.body: Bulk seed purchase lowers cost; grading raises price.

steps.title: Rules
steps.body: Check the current legal and registration requirements with the relevant authority and a chartered accountant.

activity.prompt: Tick the practical tasks an FPO promoter should complete.
items: List member farmers, land and crops
Hold a general meeting and elect a board
Prepare a business plan with costs and revenue
Open a bank account and maintain books
Identify buyers and arrange grading and storage
Seek training from agencies such as NABARD or the state agriculture department
